We're excited to announce the Mathlib Initiative, a new program under Renaissance Philanthropy, with $5M initial funding from XTX's founder Alex Gerko. See the RenPhil press release.

@Adam Topaz, @Oliver Nash and @Johan Commelin will be leading the initiative. We thank @Kim Morrison for the big role they played in forming the vision and writing the funding proposal.
We will be looking to grow the team in the next few months. The Mathlib Initiative will support Mathlib's maintenance and growth in the coming years, in coordination with the Mathlib maintainer team. In particular, we will (i) pay some people to review and triage PRs on the queue, (ii) work on scaling the infrastructure to support an ecosystem of math libraries depending on Mathlib, (iii) organise existing documentation, write new documentation, develop educational materials, (iv) create Mathlib-specific tooling for AI datasets, and hooks for AI agents to work on formal mathematics.
More precise roadmaps will follow in Fall 2025.

Although the Mathlib Initiative will work hard on reviewing PRs on the queue, it should be understood that the Mathlib maintainer team retains decision power and will remain in charge of the Mathlib library.

Parallel to this funding, Gerko also donated $5M to the Lean FRO. See #announce > Lean FRO.
Is there a discussion thread for this?
Yes: #general > Mathlib initiative annoucement discussion.

We're excited to welcome @Bryan Gin-ge Chen at the Mathlib Initiative.

Bryan did a PhD in theoretical condensed matter physics at University of Pennsylvania, and has held several positions in academia and industry. He has been formalizing mathematics and helping with the community infrastructure since 2018.

With his experience as data scientist, and his deep knowledge of everything CI-related in the Mathlib ecosystem, Bryan will work on improving the editorial workflow, and maintaining and developing the Mathlib CI.

We're excited to welcome @Anne Baanen at the Mathlib Initiative.

Anne did a PhD on formalizing algebraic number theory at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam (NL), and has been a Mathematical Research Engineer at the Lean FRO. They have been formalizing mathematics and part of this community since 2018.

Anne will work on organizing and structuring all the documentation that is available in the community, as well as reviewing (meta) PRs on the queue.

Today our website has officially gone live: https://mathlib-initiative.org/

We've also published an interview which I think is worth a look: https://www.renaissancephilanthropy.org/news-and-insights/kevin-buzzard-and-alex-kontorovich-on-the-future-of-formal-mathematics-a-mathlib-initiative-interview

I am delighted to announce several new members of the Mathlib Initiative team. Within the last week we have welcomed five new Mathematical Research Engineers: @Dagur Asgeirsson @Kenny Lau @Jireh Loreaux @Thomas Murrills @Andrew Yang

We also expect to welcome others soon!
Moments ago we just finished the paperwork to add @Robin Carlier to the team, as another Mathematical Research Engineer.

We look forward to seeing impact in the form of improved statistics for the #queue though of course, this will take some time.
We're very pleased to welcome two new people at the Mathlib Initiative. @Jon Eugster is joining the reviewer team, and @Marcelo Lynch will work on ecosystem infrastructure.

We're delighted to welcome @Paul Cadman  to the Mathlib Initiative. He joins us as a Mathematical Research Engineer with a focus on metaprogramming.

Paul has a PhD in algebraic geometry, extensive experience as a software developer, including as a compiler engineer in Rust / Haskell, and is one of the first people to develop in Lean on iOS https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/579630-Project-announcements/topic/lean-ios.20-.20build.20iOS.20apps.20with.20Lean/with/590252065.

Welcome Paul!

I am happy to announce the following developments at the Mathlib Initiative:

  • @Monica Omar has joined our Reviewer team
  • @Robin Carlier and @Brian Nugent have joined the StacksLib team (a partnership with GDM described here).
  • @Mantas Baksys, @Fabian Glöckle, and @Bhavik Mehta have joined the Formal Frontier team.

We are frequently on the look out for people to join the Reviewer team and we continue to welcome indications of interest in that role. Maintaining a list of interested candidates assists us to backfill positions quickly when people need to move on. Most of our reviewers work one day per week.
I am happy to announce that @Michael Rothgang has joined the Mathlib Initiative. His main role will be as community coordinator, assisting the Mathlib maintainer team with organizational efforts.
